10 Week English Program · Day 2 · Vocabulary · CEFR A2–B1 · 60 min

Lesson 1.2.1 Overview

Planning Events & Communicating with Others

Total Duration 60 Minutes

Welcome to Day 2! Learn to discuss a community event, exchange important details, coordinate responsibilities, and present a simple plan. Build from familiar A2 sentences toward confident B1 communication.

01. Vocabulary

Learn 12 practical event-planning and communication terms.

02. Accuracy

Use vocabulary in meaningful sentences and understand a realistic workplace-style dialogue.

03. Communication

Plan a neighborhood event with a partner and explain your decisions.

01 · WARM-UP · 5 MIN

What's a Block Party?

Cultural connection: A block party is a neighborhood gathering, often held outdoors, where people socialize, share food, and enjoy activities together.

Look at all three pictures first. Describe what you notice, then discuss with a partner. Try to add one extra detail to every answer.

Speaking tip: Try Answer + Detail. Example: “Yes, I have attended a neighborhood event. We shared food and played games.”

05 · COLLABORATIVE TASK · 15 MIN

Plan Your Block Party

Work in pairs or small groups. Plan a community event and create a short dialogue. Use at least six target words. Save your dialogue: you will use it again in Lesson 1.2.3 Expressions.

Scenario A · Event Coordinator

You organize the event and ask your partner to help with arrangements.

  • What is the venue?
  • What time will the event start?
  • What activities should we arrange?
  • Who can send the invitations?
  • When should guests RSVP?

Scenario B · Volunteer

You offer help, ask questions, and confirm your responsibilities.

  • What do you need help with?
  • Can I organize the games?
  • Who is responsible for refreshments?
  • How can we confirm attendance?
  • Could you share the schedule?

Useful sentence starters

“Let's arrange…” · “Could you confirm…?” · “I can be responsible for…” · “We should send invitations…” · “Please RSVP by…”

A: Let's plan a gathering for Saturday. Can you arrange the games?
B: Sure! I can be responsible for the activities. Have you confirmed the venue?
A: Yes, the community center. We should send invitations today.
B: Great. Let's ask everyone to RSVP by Thursday.

Event Planning Checklist

Suggested time: 10 min10:00
06 · FINAL CHALLENGE · 10 MIN

Present Your Event Plan

Present your plan in a short group presentation. Explain where the event will happen, when it will take place, what guests will do, and who is responsible for each task.

Presentation guiding questions
  1. What event are you organizing?
  2. Where and when will it take place?
  3. What activities and refreshments will you provide?
  4. How will you invite guests and confirm attendance?
  5. Who is responsible for each part of the event?
Audience follow-up questions

“Why did you choose that venue?” · “What will you do if more people attend?” · “How will you share the schedule?”

Self-Assessment

Day 2 Complete! 🎉

You've practiced planning an event, coordinating with others, and explaining responsibilities in English.
